pages.title: Steamer
pages.text: The steamer is $(thing)a multi-block structure$().$(br2)Right-click it with a $(thing)Bamboo Steamer Basket Drawer$() to add a layer, up to $(thing)four layers$() and up to $(thing)three blocks tall$(); each layer provides $(thing)four processing slots$(), so a full stack is 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 slots.$(br2)Right-click with a $(thing)Bamboo Steamer Cover$() to put the lid on; sneak and right-click with a Crowbar to take the lid off or remove a layer.$(br2)Right-click with an empty hand to open the interface and see how far each slot has got.

pages.title: How It Gets Heat
pages.text: The steamer does not burn anything itself — it needs $(thing)water and a gas cooking stove$():$(li)Put a $(thing)cauldron filled with water$() directly below the steamer$(li)Put a $(thing)lit gas cooking stove$() directly below the cauldron$(br2)It must be "stove → water cauldron → steamer" stacked vertically adjacent; with several layers, heat travels up from the bottom layer.$(br2)Without the cover it is an open pot and steaming does not progress.

pages.title: Example
pages.text: Stove at the bottom, water cauldron in the middle, steamer on top with the cover on.

pages.title: Steaming and Batching
pages.text: Each slot advances once per second, and a full progress turns the item into its result in place (the count stays the same).$(br2)Batching rule: when a slot holds $(thing)up to four items the recipe time is used$(); above four the time becomes $(thing)recipe time × count ÷ 4$() — so a stack of 64 takes 16 times as long. Split the load across slots to go faster.$(br2)Available slots and heat are re-checked every second; hoppers can insert and extract on any side.
